**Finding: missing (medium) — no post-termination transition assistance or data return.**

What I checked:
- **§ 10 (Confidentiality)** — mutual confidentiality obligations only; no return-or-destroy provision for Proprietary Information.
- **§ 13 (Term)** — puts the burden on *us*: Client must arrange a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days. It confirms we retain ownership of domains and Client Content, but ownership alone gives no delivery mechanism.
- **§ 14 (Termination)** — only fixes how long TrueLink keeps serving after our notice.
- Searches for transition/exit/return/export/deletion returned nothing.

So the Agreement leaves our borrower and loan data sitting on TrueLink's systems with no obligation to hand it back, no migration cooperation, and no deletion discipline — while §13 simultaneously makes the migration timetable our problem.

Redline (validated ok:true): a new **§ 14a** inserted after § 14 requiring TrueLink to (i) provide up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates including migration cooperation, (ii) return all Client Content, Client IP, borrower/loan data and other Client data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days of request, and (iii) delete and certify deletion thereafter. This lands on the preferred position; the fallback of 90 days' assistance with a 30-day export is flagged in the comment as a trade.

Two points worth noting for the negotiation: the new clause sits within Sections 5–30, so it survives expiry/termination under § 24 without further amendment. And because § 13 already obliges us to stand up replacement hosting within 60 days, the six-month assistance window is genuinely useful rather than cosmetic — if TrueLink pushes back to 90 days, that still comfortably covers the § 13 timetable, which is why the fallback is defensible here.
